explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/954: Rosen's sequence a_0 = 0, a_1 = 1, with a_{k+1} the least n such that #{(i,j) : 0 ≤ i ≤ j ≤ k, j ≥ 1, a_i + a_j ≤ n} < n. Is the number of solutions of a_i + a_j ≤ x equal to x + O(x^{1/4+o(1)})? rosenAux builds the sequence stage by stage, and a Python recomputation reproduces 0, 1, 3, 5, 9, 13, 17, 24, 31, 38, 45. solutionCount counts pairs with j ≤ x, which is all of them because a_j ≥ j. The statement reads O(x^{1/4+o(1)}) as O(x^{1/4+ε}) for every ε > 0, the standard reading. Faithful.
